synopsis: The booklet presents Sprague-Geers time-history error as one of several metrics for assessing simulation agreement; it compares magnitude and phase across a whole time trace [f7553, f7763]. The glossary confirms that the method used for the booklet’s reported comparison figures combines magnitude and phase terms [f14743]. Chapter 10 cites its use in FAA seat certification and gives an example acceptance guideline of 10% [f7764]. In the worked example, measured and simulated load peaks are 1,315 lb and 1,360 lb, respectively; the 3.42% peak error and 7.2% Sprague-Geers error both meet that guideline [f7781, f7782]. The supplied facts establish this threshold for the FAA example, not a general acceptance threshold for heavy off-road machine validation [f7764, f7782].

relations.note: Both describe the metric as combining magnitude and phase comparisons.
Defines the time-history metric listed among simulation-agreement measures.
Specifies the magnitude-and-phase formulation used for reported comparison figures.
Provides measured and simulated peaks and the FAA example’s resulting time-history error.
Adds peak error and confirms both errors meet the example guideline.
The within-guideline finding relies on the example’s 10% acceptance criterion.
